subject.summary: Archivists appraise, arrange, and guide the safe preservation of permanent records and materials of historical value, research archival provenance, develop classification systems, catalogs, and finding aids, maintain digital archives, implement access policies, provide reference services to researchers, and organize public education. Research uses archives as materials; archaeological excavation, osteological analysis, and engineering exploration are not core tasks of this occupation. The US BLS typical entry-level education is a master's degree; O*NET is Job Zone Five, SVP8+, and 84% of respondents answered that newly hired personnel need a master's, 6% a bachelor's, and 6% a post-master's certificate. These are answers about requirements, not the nationwide educational composition of incumbents, and not a uniform Chinese threshold. Chinese positions are governed by employer requirements and archives law; Chinese and US statistics are understood separately.
